newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares slip as profits go home.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares slip as profits go home.

text.p: Danish share prices slipped in early trade on Monday, with dealers blaming profit-taking after last week's record gains and saying that a fall in U.S. prices or fresh worries about EMU could provoke more selling.
"All it takes is some negative event or other to let loose massive profit-taking," one dealer said.
At 0810 GMT the KFX top-20 index was down 0.33 point to 172.71, while its August future was untraded at 173.85.
Danisco was expected to do well, with the share tipped by the daily newspaper Jyllands-Posten ahead of Wednesday's full-year results.
The company is expected to announce a rise in pre-tax profits of around 12.7 percent over last year. Its share was two crowns up, at 429.00 crowns on Monday morning.
Eyes were also on Carlsberg whose planned sale of its half of the Carlsberg-Tetley joint venture to Britain's Bass is expectedf to receive the verdict of British competition watchdogs this week.
At 0820 GMT its share was up five crowns, to 375.00 crowns.
BG Bank, newspaper Berlingske Tidende's share of the week although some analysts consider it overvalued, fell four crowns, to 361.00.
